preparer: Session D legal-design worker, executing rcap-hi-stage-one-court-fee-addendum
decisionSource: HRS sections 607-4 and 607-5 read in full at the Hawaii State Legislature's own publication; the Hawaii State Judiciary's published District Court Filing Fees and Costs, Circuit Court Filing Fees and Costs, and List of Civil Filing Fees; and Hawaii Rules of Penal Procedure Form B read against Form A and against the filings the Rules actually append it for. Read alongside the integrated stage-one filing-vehicle decision, the Hawaii memo and the normalized track registry.
whatThisDocumentIs: A single-question addendum to the integrated Hawaii stage-one decision. That decision narrowed the fee question as far as its own evidence allowed and left it at no_statutory_fee_established_court_cost_practice_not_conclusively_established, recording that the Judiciary publishes no filing fee for a motion in an existing penal case but that the Rules of Penal Procedure append Form B, a request to proceed without paying filing fees, which shows that some penal filings do carry a fee. This addendum answers what that record could not: it reads the Judiciary's own fee schedules and establishes affirmatively why Form B exists, which removes the one piece of contrary-looking evidence. It amends nothing, contradicts nothing, and does not restate the stage-one decision.

scopeOfThisJob.memoNote: HI.memo.json belongs to rcap-hi-expungement-stage-one-and-hcjdc-159b-memo-correction and was not opened for writing by this job.
scopeOfThisJob.questionAnswered: Whether a participant filing a stage-one expungement motion or application under HRS 706-622.5, 706-622.8, 706-622.9 or 291E-64 pays a court filing fee.

relationshipToTheIntegratedStageOneDecis.whatItHeld: That none of the five provisions imposes a fee, authorizes one or mentions a fee waiver; that the Judiciary publishes no filing fee for a motion filed in an existing penal case; that Form B shows some penal filings carry a fee, Rule 40 post-conviction proceedings being the ordinary example, and those open a new proceeding rather than moving in an existing one; and that the residue is clerk practice, at release level and not build level.
relationshipToTheIntegratedStageOneDecis.whereThisAddendumAgrees: On every point. Each of those findings was re-tested here against primary sources and each holds. In particular the record's reasoning about Form B — that it exists because Rule 40 opens a new proceeding — was an inference it drew without the fee schedules in hand, and it is correct.
relationshipToTheIntegratedStageOneDecis.whatThisAddendumAdds: Three things the stage-one record did not have. First, the exclusion in each statute is quoted and its scope fixed. Second, the Judiciary's own published fee schedules were obtained and read, and they contain no fee for any filing in an adult criminal case other than an appeal. Third, and decisively, the district court schedule prices the HRPP Rule 40 petition as a special proceeding at $155, which converts the record's inference about Form B into a documented fact and removes the only piece of evidence that pointed the other way.
relationshipToTheIntegratedStageOneDecis.disagreementDetail: Nothing in this addendum contradicts the integrated decision. The verdict moves from not_conclusively_established to established only because new evidence was obtained, not because the earlier reasoning was wrong.

controllingSources.citation: Haw. Rev. Stat. section 607-4(a), District court costs
controllingSources.verbatimText: The fees prescribed by subsection (b) shall be paid to the clerk of the district court as costs of court by the person instituting the action or proceeding, or offering the paper for filing, or causing the document to be issued or the services to be performed in the district court; provided that nothing in subsection (b) shall apply to cases of adults charged with commission of a crime, or minors referred to the district court by the family court; provided further that for the purposes of subsection (b), "judgment" includes an order from which an appeal lies; and provided further that the fees prescribed by subsection (b)(10) shall be deposited by the clerk of the district court into the judiciary computer system special fund pursuant to section 601-3.7.
controllingSources.scopeOfTheExclusion: The exclusion is drafted as a limit on the whole of subsection (b), which is the entire district-court fee schedule, and it turns on the character of the case rather than on the character of the paper. It therefore reaches a paper offered for filing in an adult criminal case as much as it reaches the institution of one, because subsection (a) applies the schedule to instituting an action, offering a paper for filing, causing a document to be issued and causing services to be performed, and disapplies all of it for such cases.

controllingSources.citation: Haw. Rev. Stat. section 607-5(a), Costs; circuit courts
controllingSources.verbatimText: The fees prescribed by the schedule in this section shall be paid to the clerk of the circuit court as costs of court by the person instituting the action or proceeding, or offering the paper for filing, or causing the document to be issued or the services to be performed in the circuit court; provided that nothing in the schedule shall apply to cases of adults charged with commission of a crime, or to proceedings under section 571-11(1), (2), or (9), to proceedings under chapter 333F or 334, to small estates including decedents' estates and protection of property of minors and persons under disability when the amount payable is fixed by another statute.
controllingSources.scopeOfTheExclusion: Identical in structure to the district-court exclusion and identical in the words that matter: 'nothing in the schedule shall apply to cases of adults charged with commission of a crime'. The disapplication is of the schedule as a whole.

controllingSources.citation: District Court Filing Fees and Costs, Hawaii State Judiciary, filing fees effective January 1, 2014, revised 12/31/2013
controllingSources.operativeFinding: The schedule lists filing of a complaint, summary possession, small claims, temporary restraining order, petition for judicial review, restitution order, demand for jury trial, appeal to appellate court civil and criminal, foreign judgments, intervention and cross-claims, and one further entry: 'HRPP Rule 40 Petition (Special Proceeding) $155.00', cited to HRPP Rule 40 and HRS 607-4(b)(1). There is no entry for a motion or an application filed in an existing adult criminal case, and the only criminal entry of any kind is the $100 appellate appeal under HRS 607-4(b)(4).

controllingSources.citation: Circuit Court Filing Fees and Costs, Hawaii State Judiciary, effective January 1, 2014, as of January 02, 2014
controllingSources.operativeFinding: Filing fees are listed for civil actions and special proceedings including those filed by prisoners at $315, jury-trial demand, transfer from district court, mechanic's and materialman's lien, foreign judgments, appeal to a circuit court, and appeals to the appellate court at $315 non-criminal and $100 criminal. Nothing is listed for a motion or an application in an existing adult criminal case. The remainder of the document is court costs — copies, certification, microfilm — not filing fees.

controllingSources.citation: List of Civil Filing Fees, Hawaii State Judiciary, updated 6/17/2022
controllingSources.operativeFinding: The Judiciary's most recently updated fee listing. Its sections are Circuit Court Civil, Conservatorship and Guardianship, Mechanic and Materialman Lien, Probate, Special Proceeding Prisoner, Trust, Regular Claims, Small Claims, Special Proceedings, Ignition Interlock Petition, DC Temporary Restraining Order, Land Court, Tax Appeal, Divorce, Civil Union, FC Agency Appeal, Adoption, Guardianship, Paternity, the two uniform family acts, Family Court Miscellaneous, Domestic Abuse and Gun Violence. It contains no criminal section, and the word 'criminal' does not appear anywhere in it. Every motion fee it lists — $30 in Circuit Court Civil and Land Court, $15 and $130 and $215 in the family-court types — sits under a civil, land or family case type.
controllingSources.whyItMatters: It is the most current schedule the Judiciary publishes and it is expressly a civil list. A criminal motion fee is not merely absent from it; the document does not reach criminal cases at all, which is what HRS 607-4(a) and 607-5(a) would predict.

controllingSources.citation: Hawaii Rules of Penal Procedure, Form A and Form B, and Rule 60 form inventory
controllingSources.operativeFinding: The Rules append thirteen forms, A through M. Form A is the Petition for Post-Conviction Relief under Rule 40 — Petition to Vacate, Set Aside, or Correct Judgment or to Release Petitioner from Custody. Form B is the Request to Proceed Without Paying Filing Fees. Form B is referenced nowhere in the Rules except inside Form A's own instructions, which read at paragraph (3): 'You must submit either the appropriate filing fees, or a Request to Proceed Without Paying Filing Fees (Form B) with this petition. Upon receipt, your petition will be filed. Your Request to Proceed Without Paying Filing Fees (Form B) will be either approved or denied after consideration by the court. If your Request to Proceed Without Paying Filing Fees (Form B) is denied, you will be notified that you must pay the filing fees in order to proceed with your petition and that, if you fail to pay, your petition will be dismissed.' Paragraph (4) adds that Form B must be signed setting forth information establishing inability to pay, with a custodial-account certificate where the petitioner is in custody. No expungement form is appended.
controllingSources.whatFormBProves: Exactly what the integrated stage-one decision inferred, and no more. Form B is the fee-waiver companion to the Rule 40 petition, and the district court schedule prices that petition as a special proceeding at $155. A Rule 40 petition opens a new proceeding attacking a judgment; a stage-one expungement application or motion is filed in the participant's own existing criminal case and opens nothing. Form B is therefore evidence that a new penal special proceeding carries a fee, and is not evidence that a filing in an existing adult criminal case does.

sourcesExpresslyNotRelieduponAsProof: No commercial compilation was used to establish any text.

The absence of a criminal motion fee from a Judiciary schedule is not relied on alone. Absence from a document that describes itself as a summary would be weak; the finding rests first on the statutory exclusion, which is affirmative, and the schedules corroborate it.
No county or single-circuit practice note, clerk handout or telephone enquiry was used. None was obtained.

determination.2_whichOfTheFourItIs: Not charged, rather than charged, waived or unestablished. It is not 'charged'. It is not 'waived', which would presuppose a fee that exists and is excused on a showing — nothing is excused here because the schedules do not reach the case in the first place, and no waiver application arises. And it is no longer 'unestablished': the statutory exclusion is affirmative rather than a silence, both Judiciary schedules were read rather than merely not found to contain an entry, and the one artifact that pointed the other way is now explained.
determination.3_theStatutoryBasis: HRS 607-5(a) disapplies the whole circuit-court schedule, and HRS 607-4(a) disapplies the whole district-court schedule, to 'cases of adults charged with commission of a crime'. A stage-one expungement application or motion under HRS 706-622.5(4), 706-622.5(5), 706-622.8, 706-622.9(3) or 291E-64(e) is a paper offered for filing in the participant's own adult criminal case. Both statutes reach papers offered for filing and not only the institution of an action, so the exclusion applies to the filing itself.
determination.4_whyTheStatuteAndTheScheduleAgree: They are the same rule seen twice. The Judiciary's schedules are the operational expression of chapter 607, and they cite it: the district schedule cites HRS 607-4(b)(1), 607-4(b)(2), 607-4(b)(3), 607-4(b)(4) and 607-4(b)(10) line by line. A schedule built on subsection (b) cannot charge a case that subsection (a) removes from subsection (b).

5_whatIsNotDecidedByThisAnswer.hcjdcStageTwoFee: A different fee, and it is real. The Hawaii Criminal Justice Data Center charges $35 for a first-time expungement, $50 for a non-first-time expungement and $20 for a duplicate certificate, each including a non-refundable $10 processing fee, payable only by United States cashier's check or money order to the State of Hawaii. It is an executive-agency fee for the stage-two HCJDC 159(b) application, not a court fee, and nothing in HRS 607-4 or 607-5 touches it. A packet must not merge the two: the correct participant-facing statement is that the court stage costs nothing and the agency stage costs $35 or $50.
5_whatIsNotDecidedByThisAnswer.serviceAndCopyCosts: Not filing fees and not excluded by chapter 607's criminal-case proviso in the same way. Copies of a document in a public record maintained by the clerk are charged under RCCH Rule 2.2 and RDCH Rule 2.2 at $1.00 for the first page and $0.50 for each additional page in the clerk's office, $5.00 plus copying from off-site storage, and $5.00 plus $1.00 per page on microfilm, with certification of a copy at $2.00. Postage for service by mail is the participant's own cost. These arise only if the participant chooses to obtain certified copies or serves by mail, they are not a precondition of filing, and they are small. They should be named as costs the participant may incur rather than folded into a fee statement.
5_whatIsNotDecidedByThisAnswer.whatTheParticipantStillPays: In the ordinary case: nothing to the court at stage one; postage to serve the prosecuting attorney; whatever a certified copy of the signed order costs if the participant needs one to attach to the HCJDC application; and the HCJDC fee at stage two.

determination.6_clerkPractice: One question remains and it is genuinely open. Whether a clerk would accept a filing under the original criminal case number in a case closed before July 1, 2004, which is the population HRS 706-622.8 addresses, or before June 22, 2006, which is the population HRS 706-622.9(4) addresses, or would instead require a new proceeding to be opened. It matters because it is the only path by which a fee could arise: a new civil special proceeding would attract $315 in the circuit court under the 2014 schedule, or $155 in the district court. Nothing located requires it, no statute or rule contemplates it, and the statutes direct the application to the court that sentenced. This is recorded as unresolved rather than answered in the participant's favour.
determination.7_doesThisChangeTheGeneratedPleading: No. Nothing about the vehicle, the caption, the allegations, the signature, the service or the proposed order turns on the fee. The five stage-one pleadings are specified and generable without this answer, and neither the Hawaii memo correction nor the Hawaii custom-pleading job waits on it.
determination.8_blockerClassification: release_blocker_not_build_blocker. It is participant-facing copy and a filing instruction. The integrated stage-one decision classified it the same way and that classification is unchanged; what changes is that the copy can now be written.

affectedTracks.effectOnEach: Identical. The answer is a single common finding, because the exclusion turns on the character of the case rather than on which of the four statutes supplies the remedy, and all five routes are filed in an adult criminal case. Two of the five sit disproportionately in the clerk-practice residual, because HRS 706-622.8 and HRS 706-622.9(4) reach sentences imposed more than twenty and nearly twenty years ago respectively.
affectedTracks.courtLevel: The exclusion applies in both court levels, so the answer does not change with the grade of the underlying offence. A class C felony route disposed of in the circuit court and a section 712-1249 or section 291E-64 route disposed of in the district court are both excluded, by section 607-5(a) and section 607-4(a) respectively.
affectedTracks.tracksNotAffected: hi_nonconviction_expungement, hi_dag_danc_expungement, hi_712_1200_deferred_expungement and hi_state_initiated_marijuana_pilot are outside this question. The first three are stage-two or agency routes whose fee is the HCJDC fee, and the fourth is a state-initiated pilot with no participant filing.

itemsSupplied: rules.fees on each of the five tracks can state: no court filing fee at stage one, because HRS 607-5(a) and HRS 607-4(a) exclude cases of adults charged with commission of a crime from the circuit and district court fee schedules; an HCJDC fee of $35 first-time or $50 non-first-time applies at stage two.

rules.feeWaiver on each of the five can state that no waiver arises because no fee is charged, and that HRPP Form B is the fee-waiver companion to a Rule 40 post-conviction petition and must not be placed in an expungement packet.
The existing release-level unresolved question 'Any court filing fee at stage one is unresolved' can be replaced by the narrower clerk-practice question recorded in determination 6.
A cost line naming postage and, where needed, the clerk's certified-copy charge, kept separate from the fee statement.
memoConsequenceHandedOff.notPerformedHere: This addendum owns only its own record. It did not open HI.memo.json.

residualQuestions.question: Whether a clerk will accept a stage-one filing under the original criminal case number in a case closed before July 1, 2004 or before June 22, 2006, or would require a new proceeding, which is the only route by which a fee could arise.
residualQuestions.missingAuthority: Judiciary clerk practice, which is not published. No statute, rule or schedule addresses it and none was found to require a new proceeding.

residualQuestions.question: The two itemised Judiciary schedules carry 2013 and 2014 dates. The most recently updated listing, of 6/17/2022, is expressly civil and has no criminal section.
residualQuestions.analysis: Low consequence. The determination rests on the statutory exclusion, which is current at the 2026-01-05 compilation, and the schedules corroborate rather than carry it. A newer schedule could not create a criminal filing fee without an amendment to HRS 607-4 or 607-5, and none has occurred.

residualQuestions.question: The district schedule's civil entries each carry a $35 Indigent Legal Services Surcharge under HRS 607-5.7 and a $20 administrative fee under HRS 607-4(b)(10). Whether either could attach to a criminal-case filing was not separately researched.
residualQuestions.analysis: Both are pinned to subsection (b) entries, and subsection (a) disapplies subsection (b) to adult criminal cases, so on the face of the statute neither attaches. Recorded because it was not traced through HRS 607-5.7's own text.

terminalDispositionDetail.why: The narrowest accurate result. It is not 'unestablished', because the exclusion is affirmative statutory text, both fee schedules were obtained and read, and the single contrary-looking artifact is explained. It is not 'waived', because no fee exists to excuse. And it is not unqualified, because one clerk-practice question survives and it is the only route by which a fee could arise.
terminalDispositionDetail.evidenceDirection: Every source read pointed the same way. The answer was not chosen for convenience: the one artifact that appeared to cut against it, HRPP Form B, was pursued to the schedule that prices the petition it belongs to, and it turned out to support the conclusion rather than qualify it.
